record.question: Which of the following observations is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942?
options: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi
It did not attract the labour class in general
record.explanation: Verified on printed page 3 of '3.Inspector of Taxes 2016 General Studies Paper I.pdf' (Jan 2016, MPSC): Q21 reads exactly as in the bank with options (a) non-violent movement, (b) led by Mahatma Gandhi, (c) spontaneous movement, (d) did not attract the labour class in general. The Quit India Movement was launched by Gandhi on 8 August 1942 as a non-violent 'do or die' satyagraha, and it spread rapidly as a spontaneous mass movement; it also drew in the working class, with Bombay textile-mill workers (including Tata mills), railway staff and workers in other industrial centres going on strike and being arrested, so the claim that it did not attract the labour class is the observation that is not true.
